access_continuity_justification: Single maintainer: no second account holds write or release authority, there is no documented escrow of credentials or sessions, and no successor is named, so the project stops if that person disappears. CONTRIBUTING.md 'Governance and roles' states this openly. The fix is a co-maintainer, which is a people problem, not a document.
achieve_passing_justification: The project holds the passing badge, earned 2026-11-18: https://www.bestpractices.dev/projects/16895
assurance_case_justification: docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md is the assurance case: a threat description with the trust boundary and each actor and what it can inject, the identified attack surface analysed sink by sink, the controls that mitigate each (React escaping, zero runtime dependencies, actions pinned to commit SHAs, least-privilege workflow tokens, OIDC signing, audit and OSV gates, CodeQL, branch protection, private disclosure), and the residual risks that remain unmitigated. https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/blob/main/docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md
automated_integration_testing_justificat: The suite runs on every pull request and every push to main through .github/workflows/ci.yml; its build job (tests with coverage, both builds, package-payload check) is a required status check that reports success or failure on the commit, and publish-npm.yml runs the suite and the audits again before any release. https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
build_common_tools_justification: npm scripts plus Vite and the TypeScript compiler; no bespoke build tooling.
build_floss_tools_justification: Every tool in the chain is free software (Node.js, npm, Vite, esbuild, TypeScript, Vitest); no proprietary build step is required.
build_justification: npm run build (tsc --noEmit then vite build for the docs site) and npm run build:lib (ESM bundle, style.css and .d.ts) build everything from a clean checkout with npm ci; both run in CI on every pull request: https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/actions/workflows/ci.yml
build_non_recursive_justification: One package, one entry. 'vite build --config vite.lib.config.ts' walks src/index.ts once and 'tsc -p tsconfig.lib.json' emits the declarations; there are no subdirectories with their own build and no cross-dependency between build units to order.
build_repeatable_justification: Measured on 2026-11-18: two clean 'npm run build:lib' runs from the same package-lock.json, with dist/ deleted between them, produced 16 files with identical sha256 per file (documented in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md: https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md). Stated scope: same lockfile, toolchain and machine; hermetic cross-machine reproducibility is the separate build_reproducible criterion and is not met.
build_standard_variables_justification: No native compilation happens: the toolchain is Node.js, Vite, esbuild and the TypeScript compiler, configured through vite.lib.config.ts and tsconfig.lib.json. There is no CC, CFLAGS, CXX, CXXFLAGS or LDFLAGS for a build system to honour.
code_of_conduct_justification: A condensed Contributor Covenant is published in a standard location, with a private reporting channel and a commitment to state the outcome once a case is closed. https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/blob/main/.github/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md
coding_standards_enforced_justification: Nothing enforces a style automatically: ci.yml has no ESLint or Prettier step. It fails on type errors, on advisory findings and on coverage below the thresholds, but a style deviation merges green.
coding_standards_justification: No coding style guide is named and no formatter or linter is configured. What is enforced today is the TypeScript compiler (strict, noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters, noFallthroughCasesInSwitch) plus the layout rules in CONTRIBUTING.md 'Rules of the kit', which is not the same as a stated style standard.
crypto_call_justification: No cryptographic calls exist in src/; the package has no runtime dependencies either.
crypto_certificate_verification_justific: The software does not use TLS and opens no network connections, so there is no certificate for it to verify. Transport security belongs to the registry, to GitHub Pages for the docs site and to the embedding application.
crypto_credential_agility_justification: The project handles no authentication credentials and no private keys: there is no login, no token and no key material anywhere in the package. The only client-side state is the selected skin under the localStorage key 'nc-theme'.
crypto_floss_justification: No cryptographic functionality to implement with free software.
crypto_password_storage_justification: No authentication data at all. The only client-side storage is the selected skin under the localStorage key nc-theme (docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md).
crypto_pfs_justification: The project opens no network connections; transport security is the registry's and the browser's.
crypto_published_justification: The kit performs no cryptographic operations: no hashing, signing, cipher, key exchange or random generation of its own. Signing and hashing that protect releases happen in npm and Sigstore, outside the shipped code.
crypto_random_justification: The shipped code requests no random values (no Math.random or crypto.getRandomValues in src/).
crypto_verification_private_justificatio: Same reason: the kit sends no requests, so it never puts private information in an HTTP header or a query string.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: No cryptography in the shipped code, so no algorithm or mode choice to review.
crypto_working_justification: The project implements no cryptographic algorithm.
delivery_unsigned_justification: npm delivery is HTTPS with a sha512 integrity per version, a registry signature and a SLSA v1 provenance attestation; each GitHub Release additionally carries the Sigstore bundle (.sigstore.json) and the in-toto statement (.intoto.jsonl) for its tarball.
dependency_monitoring_justification: Dependabot security and version updates are configured (.github/dependabot.yml) with Dependabot alerts enabled, and CI fails on advisories at two levels: 'npm audit --omit=dev' for the shipped surface and 'npm run audit:deps' (OSV) across the whole tree, so a development-only advisory blocks a release as well. https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/blob/main/.github/dependabot.yml
documentation_achievements_justification: The front page links the achievements: OpenSSF Best Practices 'passing' and OpenSSF Baseline level 1 (added the day the confirmation email arrived), alongside the OpenSSF Scorecard badge. https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui#readme
documentation_architecture_justification: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md describes the layer order and its one-way dependency direction, the theming mechanism (a block of CSS custom properties per skin, switched by one attribute), the two builds from one source tree, the public surface and how it is verified. https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
documentation_basics_justification: User and API documentation lives in the repository and on the site: README.md (install, quick start, the four skins), docs/COMPONENTS.md (every exported component), docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (design), docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md (trust boundary), docs/VERIFYING_A_RELEASE.md (provenance checks), GUIA_DE_USO.md (Spanish) and the hosted docs site https://dan-netrunner.github.io/night-city-ui/
documentation_current_justification: docs/COMPONENTS.md documents every export reachable from src/index.ts against the shipped version (0.1.4), GUIA_DE_USO.md carries the Spanish guide, and CONTRIBUTING.md requires documentation to change in the same pull request as the behaviour it describes. No documentation defect is open against the current release.
documentation_quick_start_justification: The README's Install section plus the ThemeProvider snippet take a new user from 'npm install night-city-ui' to a rendered panel on one screen, and the docs site repeats it as a Guide page and an interactive Playground. https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui#install
documentation_roadmap_justification: No roadmap exists. The repository records what shipped (CHANGELOG.md) and the badge entry records what is missing (no dynamic analysis, no second reviewer, no continuity plan, no style enforcement), but nothing states what the project intends to do or not do over the next year.
documentation_security_justification: docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md states what a user can and cannot expect: the trust boundary (the application is trusted, its data is not), the actors and what each can inject, the assets handled (none over the network; one localStorage key), the attack surface with the analysis of each reachable sink, and an explicit list of what is out of scope. https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/blob/main/docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: There is no runtime assertion mechanism to enable in the shipped build; assertions live in the test suite (vitest expectations) instead.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis is executed, so there are no dynamic findings to fix; the automated suite and CodeQL are what gate changes.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No dynamic analysis or fuzzing harness runs today. The closest is a property-based fast-check test over Progress; a coverage-guided fuzz target is not applicable to a CSS-and-markup component kit, but DOM-level property tests could be added.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: Nothing to instrument: the codebase is TypeScript compiled to JavaScript and runs in a browser or bundler, with no memory-unsafe language in the dependency graph.
enhancement_responses_justification: Same as report_responses: no enhancement requests have been filed, nothing pending; feature_request.yml defines the channel and closed pull requests show the response path in use.
external_dependencies_justification: Every dependency is declared in package.json and pinned in the committed package-lock.json, both computer-processable - CI reads the lockfile to gate development dependencies too. The published surface has zero runtime dependencies; react and react-dom are peers >=18. https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/blob/main/package-lock.json
governance_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Governance and roles' documents how decisions are made (a change is proposed as a pull request, review feedback is adopted or declined by the maintainer, the maintainer merges or closes, disagreements are answered in the thread with the reason) and who holds authority. https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#governance-and-roles
implement_secure_design_justification: docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md reduces the surface by construction and the code matches it: no network I/O, no eval, new Function, document.write, innerHTML or dangerouslySetInnerHTML anywhere on the published surface (grep over src/components/*.tsx and src/theme.tsx returns zero matches), content rendered as escaped text nodes, one localStorage key for the theme inside a try/catch, and zero runtime dependencies. https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/blob/main/docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md
input_validation_justification: The kit validates nothing at runtime, and documents that as a deliberate boundary: docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md states 'validates nothing about the data you render' and 'URL-scheme validation is out of scope by design'. An application passing an untrusted href to a navigation item can still produce a javascript: link. Closing this means an optional scheme allowlist on the href/src props, not another paragraph.
installation_common_justification: 'npm install night-city-ui' and 'npm uninstall night-city-ui', from the public registry, with no install scripts: the package declares an allowScripts policy and the tarball carries only build output plus README, CHANGELOG and LICENSE (19 files). https://www.npmjs.com/package/night-city-ui
installation_development_quick_justifica: 'npm ci' then 'npm run dev' serves the docs site with the workbench; 'npm test' and 'npm run test:coverage' run the suite; 'npm run build' and 'npm run build:lib' reproduce both artifacts. Documented in CONTRIBUTING.md. https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#get-set-up
installation_standard_variables_justific: Nothing is written to system paths. The artifact is an ESM module and a stylesheet that the consuming application's bundler resolves, so there is no prefix or DESTDIR convention for an installer to honour.
know_common_errors_justification: docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md names the reachable sinks for a component kit and the corresponding failure classes: XSS through raw HTML (the kit never uses dangerouslySetInnerHTML, innerHTML, document.write, eval or new Function, verified by grep), URL scheme handling in href/src props, and supply-chain risk (zero runtime dependencies, committed lockfile, allow-listed install scripts, OIDC publishing with provenance).
know_secure_design_justification: docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md defines the trust boundary (the app is trusted, its data is not), the actors and what each can inject, the assets handled (none over the network, one localStorage key) and what is explicitly out of scope.
maintenance_or_update_justification: Releases follow semantic versioning and every published version stays installable from the registry, so an application pinned to an older release keeps working and can move forward reading one CHANGELOG entry at a time; breaking changes are documented per release. https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credential has ever been committed: the tree has no .npmrc or token file, publishing uses OIDC trusted publishing so no npm token exists in the repository, and GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enabled on the repo.
osps_ac_01_01_justification: GitHub enforces multi-factor authentication on the account that administers this repository (passkey or TOTP at each sign-in).
osps_ac_02_01_justification: Collaborators are added manually by the owner with an explicit role; tokens in use are fine-grained and scoped to this repository only.
osps_ac_03_01_justification: Branch protection on main requires a pull request with 2 approving reviews and required status checks (build, Analyze javascript-typescript, Analyze actions); the sole owner keeps an admin override, recorded in each merged PR.
osps_ac_03_02_justification: allow_deletions and allow_force_pushes are disabled on main, so removing it needs an explicit typed confirmation.
osps_ac_04_01_justification: The workflow token defaults to read-only and every workflow sets an explicit top-level permissions block.
osps_ac_04_02_justification: contents:write appears only on the job that pushes gh-pages and the job that creates releases; the rest are read-only, with id-token and attestations scoped to the jobs that need them.
osps_br_01_01_justification: No pull_request_target and no event fields interpolated into shell; CodeQL analyses the workflow files and OpenSSF Dangerous-Workflow scores 10.
osps_br_01_03_justification: Pull requests from forks run with no repository secrets and a read-only token; publishing and release jobs run only on main or on version tags.
osps_br_01_04_justification: Merged changes must pass review and required checks; workflow inputs (release tag) are quoted and validated against the existing release.
osps_br_02_01_justification: Semantic versions 0.1.0 through 0.1.4, unique on the registry; 0.1.1 to 0.1.4 are also tagged in git (0.1.0 predates the tagging habit).
osps_br_02_02_justification: All assets are named night-city-ui-VERSION.tgz plus .cdx.json, .sigstore.json and .intoto.jsonl, and report their sha256 digests.
osps_br_03_01_justification: Every official URI (npm registry, GitHub Pages site, repository, issue tracker) is HTTPS, and Pages has HTTPS enforcement enabled.
osps_br_03_02_justification: TLS with certificate validation; npm additionally checks each tarball against its sha512 integrity value and the registry signature.
osps_br_04_01_justification: CHANGELOG.md (Keep a Changelog) is maintained per version and now ships inside the tarball.
osps_br_05_01_justification: npm with a committed package-lock.json, installed with npm ci in CI and at publish time.
osps_br_06_01_justification: Each GitHub Release carries a Sigstore bundle and an in-toto statement; the tarball digest matches the npm artifact byte for byte.
osps_br_07_01_justification: Secret scanning with push protection is enabled; the tree contains no credentials or .npmrc, and publishing uses OIDC so no npm token exists.
osps_br_07_02_justification: SECURITY.md has a secrets and credentials policy covering storage, rotation, allow-listed install scripts and the leak response.
osps_do_01_01_justification: Guide and Playground pages on the docs site plus the README quickstart and docs/COMPONENTS.md API reference.
osps_do_02_01_justification: Issue templates for bugs and features, linked from the README; SECURITY.md covers the security-specific route.
osps_do_03_01_justification: docs/VERIFYING_A_RELEASE.md walks through registry signature, sha512 integrity and the provenance attestation.
osps_do_03_02_justification: The same guide shows how the attestation names the repository, workflow file, ref and commit that produced the artifact.
osps_do_04_01_justification: SECURITY.md supported-versions table states 0.1.x is supported and only the latest release receives fixes.
osps_do_05_01_justification: SECURITY.md states that superseded and unpublished versions are unsupported and affected ones are deprecated on npm.
osps_do_06_01_justification: SECURITY.md documents the dependency and licence thresholds; CONTRIBUTING.md forbids new runtime dependencies; Dependabot opens grouped updates weekly.
osps_do_07_01_justification: README Development and CONTRIBUTING list install, dev, test and both builds with the toolchain versions CI uses.
osps_gv_01_01_justification: CODEOWNERS names the account holding repository and release authority; SECURITY.md states releases are maintainer only.
osps_gv_01_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md describes contributor, reviewer and maintainer duties, including who may bump versions.
osps_gv_02_01_justification: GitHub Issues and the pull request review threads are open to anyone.
osps_gv_03_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md explains fork, branch, pull request, the protected main branch and who cuts releases.
osps_gv_03_02_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md rules of the kit plus the pull request template checklist.
osps_gv_04_01_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md: trust is earned through reviewed pull requests and permissions are granted manually at the lowest level.
osps_le_01_01_justification: No per-commit legal assertion is enforced today (no DCO sign-off or ICA). Contributions are covered by GitHub Terms section D.6 and the CONTRIBUTING license notice; adding a sign-off check would close this.
osps_le_02_01_justification: MIT, an OSI-approved license, in LICENSE and declared in package.json.
osps_le_02_02_justification: Releases are the same MIT-licensed source; LICENSE is inside the published npm tarball.
osps_le_03_01_justification: LICENSE file at the repository root.
osps_le_03_02_justification: The npm tarball ships LICENSE and README next to dist/ (verified with npm pack --dry-run).
osps_qa_01_02_justification: Full commit history with author, date and diff is public, including every merged pull request.
osps_qa_02_01_justification: package.json declares no runtime dependencies (React is a peer); package-lock.json pins the development toolchain and is committed.
osps_qa_02_02_justification: No compiled or native assets are released (transpiled JS and CSS). A CycloneDX SBOM is attached to every release anyway.
osps_qa_03_01_justification: build, Analyze javascript-typescript and Analyze actions are required status checks on main.
osps_qa_04_01_justification: Single-repository project; there are no other codebases to list.
osps_qa_04_02_justification: Single-repository project, so there are no subprojects to hold to the same bar.
osps_qa_05_01_justification: Only source is tracked; dist/ and node_modules are git-ignored and built in CI.
osps_qa_05_02_justification: No binaries in the default branch. The generated gh-pages deployment branch holds build output only (site JS/CSS and latin woff2 webfonts from packages pinned in the lockfile).
osps_qa_06_01_justification: The required build check runs the Vitest suite on every pull request and before publishing.
osps_qa_06_02_justification: README and CONTRIBUTING run the suite with npm test; vitest.config.ts pins the jsdom environment and ci.yml (Node 22) plus publish-npm.yml (Node 24) run it automatically.
osps_qa_06_03_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires a new or updated test with every behavioural change, and the pull request template repeats it as a checklist item.
osps_qa_07_01_justification: main requires 2 approving reviews, but with a single maintainer who cannot approve their own work, merges currently happen through an admin override, so a non-author approval is not always enforced. A second maintainer or an organization with a bypass list would close this.
osps_sa_01_01_justification: docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md tabulates actors and actions: end user, developer, contributor, CI, registry, Sigstore.
osps_sa_02_01_justification: docs/COMPONENTS.md documents every export with its props, types, rendered element and ARIA behaviour.
osps_sa_03_01_justification: docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md records the assessment, with the grep evidence behind each claim.
osps_sa_03_02_justification: docs/SECURITY_MODEL.md analyses the attack surface (React-rendered text, URL-taking props, theme authoring, supply chain) and states what is out of scope.
osps_vm_01_01_justification: SECURITY.md is a coordinated disclosure policy with reporting route, timelines and version support.
osps_vm_02_01_justification: SECURITY.md names the maintainer and the private advisory route at /security/advisories/new.
osps_vm_03_01_justification: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled on the repository and linked from SECURITY.md.
osps_vm_04_01_justification: Advisories are published as GitHub Security Advisories and mirrored in the CHANGELOG Security section; none issued so far.
osps_vm_04_02_justification: There are no dependency findings that do not affect this project: the package has zero runtime dependencies.
osps_vm_05_01_justification: SECURITY.md defines the threshold: high or critical advisories on what consumers install block a release.
osps_vm_05_02_justification: The publish workflow fails before npm publish if the audit gate reports a violation.
osps_vm_05_03_justification: npm run audit:deps checks every locked package, development included, against OSV.dev on each change, with --self-test so a dead detector cannot pass.
osps_vm_06_01_justification: SECURITY.md states the SAST threshold: high or critical CodeQL findings on main are fixed before the next release.
osps_vm_06_02_justification: CodeQL (security-and-quality) runs on push, pull request and weekly, and its checks are required to merge into main.
regression_tests_added50_justification: Honest count, over the last six months (the repository is two weeks old): two fixes to shipped behaviour. PR #7 (accessibility and best-practice failures) landed with assertions; PR #19 (the header reflowing when the theme changes) did not. That is exactly 50%, so it is recorded here as Unmet rather than argued into Met.
report_archive_justification: GitHub retains the full issue and pull request history publicly, including deleted comments' activity entries: https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/issues?q=is%3Aissue
report_responses_justification: The tracker holds no unanswered bug reports: every item in https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/issues is a pull request (21, all closed), no bug report has been filed to date, so nothing has been left without a response.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues is enabled with bug_report.yml and feature_request.yml templates, linked from README.md and SECURITY.md.
roles_responsibilities_justification: The same section names each role and what it is responsible for - maintainer (roadmap, accepting changes, releases, security response, the badge answers), contributor (proposals only, no merge rights), reporter (private disclosure) - and says who holds it; CODEOWNERS maps every path to that account ('* @dan-netrunner'). https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#governance-and-roles
signed_releases_justification: Every release is signed and the verification path is documented for a third party. npm publishes through OIDC trusted publishing - no token exists in any secret - and carries SLSA v1 provenance; each GitHub Release additionally attaches the Sigstore bundle (.sigstore.json) and the extracted in-toto statement (.intoto.jsonl), whose subject digest equals the tarball digest, plus the CycloneDX SBOM. docs/VERIFYING_A_RELEASE.md walks through checking all of it. https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/releases
sites_password_security_justification: No project site stores passwords for external users. The code is on GitHub, the docs on GitHub Pages and the package in the npm registry, and the library itself has no login, no session and no credential store.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's javascript/typescript rules cover the common web vulnerability classes relevant here (XSS through raw HTML sinks, prototype pollution, unsafe eval-likes, injection in workflow files).
static_analysis_fixed_justification: The Security tab shows zero open code scanning alerts, and the CodeQL checks are required to merge into main.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL with the security-and-quality query suite over javascript-typescript and the workflow files, on push, on pull request and weekly, publishing SARIF to the Security tab: https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/actions/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_often_justification: CodeQL runs on every pull request, on every push to main and on a weekly schedule; OpenSSF Scorecard runs on every push to main and weekly.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: The required 'build' check in https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/actions/workflows/ci.yml runs the suite with coverage on every pull request and every push to main, and publish-npm.yml runs it again before any release. A run showing the published coverage table: https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/actions/runs/44398978232
test_invocation_justification: One command runs the whole suite: 'npm test' (vitest run), with 'npm run test:coverage' for the measured run. Both are declared in package.json and documented in README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md, and CI executes the coverage form on every pull request: https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/actions/workflows/ci.yml
test_justification: Vitest suite with @testing-library/react over the shipped components and the theme provider; 34 tests, 3 files, run by npm test.
test_most_justification: Coverage over the shipped surface (src/components/*.tsx and src/theme.tsx) is 92.99% statements, 84.03% branches, 91.8% functions, measured by CI on every pull request.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states that any behavioural change must add or update a test in the same pull request and that every new component needs at least one test asserting its accessible role or label.
test_policy_mandated_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Testing' states the policy: any behavioural change must add or update a test in the same pull request, and every new component needs at least one test asserting its accessible role or label. The thresholds in vitest.config.ts make it measurable and CI makes it blocking. https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#testing
test_statement_coverage80_justification: 92.99% statement coverage (146/157) over the shipped surface - src/components/*.tsx and src/theme.tsx - measured with @vitest/coverage-v8 by 'npm run test:coverage' and enforced in CI at a 90% floor with pipefail, so the number cannot drop silently. Run with the published table: https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/actions/runs/44398978232
tests_are_added_justification: Functional changes in this repository arrive with tests: PR #8 added a property-based test for Progress alongside the Scorecard fixes, PR #3 introduced the suite for the kit and ThemeProvider, and the coverage threshold prevents later changes from reducing it.
tests_documented_added_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md 'Testing' and 'Keeping the badge honest' sections, plus the checklist in .github/pull_request_template.md.
two_person_review_justification: With one maintainer no pull request can be reviewed by a second person. Merges are done with admin rights past the two-review rule, and the entry records that instead of claiming reviews happened.
updateable_reused_components_justificati: No code is vendored or forked. Everything reused arrives from the registry as a normal devDependency or a peer dependency and is tracked in the lockfile, so an upstream fix is a Dependabot pull request rather than a manual diff against a copy.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: Nothing outstanding. Any high or critical advisory on the dependency surface blocks a release (npm audit --omit=dev and npm run audit:deps in CI), and SECURITY.md records the one advisory that ever appeared in the tree plus why it was not reachable.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No publicly known vulnerability affects the released software: OSV and the GitHub advisory database return zero entries for night-city-ui and the package has no runtime dependencies. OpenSSF Scorecard reports Vulnerabilities=10 (0 existing vulnerabilities).
vulnerability_report_credit_justificatio: No vulnerability report has been received or resolved in the last 12 months, so there is no reporter to credit. SECURITY.md is where credit would be recorded, and private reporting is enabled.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled on the repository, so a reporter can open a confidential report instead of a public issue; no PGP key is needed because the reports are private in the tracker: https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md documents how to report a vulnerability (private advisory form), what happens next and the acknowledgement window: https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received, so no response time can be measured. The committed targets in SECURITY.md (acknowledge within a week, then fix or explain) apply from the first report.
vulnerability_response_process_justifica: SECURITY.md documents the process end to end: report privately through the advisory form, acknowledgement within a week, then a fix or an explicit 'won't fix, here is why', with the embargo respected until release. https://github.com/dan-netrunner/night-city-ui/blob/main/SECURITY.md
warnings_fixed_justification: Type and lint diagnostics block the required build check, so nothing is merged carrying them; the strict compiler settings are in tsconfig.json.
warnings_justification: The default build is warning-free: tsc runs with strict, noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters and noFallthroughCasesInSwitch and CI fails on any diagnostic (npm run build is tsc --noEmit && vite build).
warnings_strict_justification: TypeScript strict mode plus the unused/fallthrough checks, and CodeQL with the security-and-quality query suite over both the source and the workflow files.
